stemBlocks.value: Rewrite the quadratic expression 5x² − 20x − 1 by completing the square, in the form a(x + h)² + k.
Think first: The constant is negative here, so keep careful track of signs when you combine it with the correction term.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p102-q08 from workbook page 102.

solutionSteps.instruction: Factor 5 out of the terms containing x.
Complete the square inside the bracket.

contentBlocks.value: half of −4 is −2, and (−2)² = 4, so x² − 4x = (x − 2)² − 4

strategyBlocks.value: Factor 5 from the x-terms, complete the square inside the bracket, expand the 5 back and combine with the −1.

whyThisWorks.value: Every quadratic can be written as a scaled square plus a constant, because a(x + h)² + k expands to ax² + 2ahx + ah² + k and the three coefficients can always be matched. Here a = 5 forces 2ah = −20, so h = −2, and then k absorbs whatever is left over. Nothing is added to the expression — the −21 exactly balances the extra 20 the square introduced.

commonErrors.misconception: Multiplying only the (x − 2)² by 5 and leaving the −4 unscaled.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Multiplying only the (x − 2)² by 5 and leaving the −4 unscaled.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing (x + 2)² because the 4 in the correction is positive.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing (x + 2)² because the 4 in the correction is positive.

examTip.value: Read off h as half the x-coefficient inside the bracket, with the same sign — the sign of h never comes from the constant term.
